title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Wish people a happy festival, birthday or wedding, understand the blessings elders give you, invite people and insist they come, and know what to do at Dashain, Tihar and a Nepali wedding.
intro:
Nepal's calendar is packed with festivals, and wedding season fills the streets with brass bands and processions. This unit gives you what you'll say and hear at all of them: **दसैंको शुभकामना!**, the blessings an elder gives you with your tika (**सधैँ खुसी रहनू**), invitations that won't take no for an answer (**पक्का आउनू है!**, **आउनै पर्छ!**) and what to say to a bride and groom.

The grammar is the language of wishing — **-को शुभकामना**, **होस्**, **-नू** — plus ways to say 'be sure to…', and the right verb for each festival: you **celebrate** Dashain (मनाउनु), **play** Holi (खेल्नु) and **receive** tika (थाप्नु).

vocab.note: चाड 'festival' + पर्व 'holy day'; used as one word for festivals in general.
Nepal's biggest festival (Sept–Oct), 15 days; tika from elders on the tenth day. Also spelt दशैं.
Five days, about three weeks after Dashain.
The last day of Tihar, when sisters put tika on their brothers.
Women's festival (Aug–Sept): red clothes, fasting, singing and dancing.
The festival of colours, in spring. Also फागु.

vocab.note: Elders give it with Dashain tika; you also give it to priests.

vocab.en: barley shoots worn with Dashain tika

दियो बाल्नु 'to light a lamp'. Same spelling as दियो 'gave'.
माला लगाउनु 'to garland someone'.
देउसी खेल्नु 'to go deusi-singing'; girls' version: भैलो.

vocab.en: mehendi (henna; the henna party before a wedding)
vermilion (red powder worn by married women)

Also उपहार (unit 16).

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings: -को शुभकामना, होस्, -नू
grammar.body:
Unit 18 introduced the wish forms **-ओस्** ('may he / it…') and **होस्** ('may it be'). At festivals, weddings and birthdays they are everywhere, together with a few fixed phrases.

**1. 'Happy X!' = X-को शुभकामना.** **दसैंको शुभकामना!**, **जन्मदिनको शुभकामना!**, **नयाँ वर्षको शुभकामना!**. Make it bigger with **धेरै धेरै**, or in writing with **हार्दिक**: 'विजया दशमीको हार्दिक मंगलमय शुभकामना' is on every card and social-media post at Dashain. Young people also simply say **ह्याप्पी दसैं!**, **ह्याप्पी बर्थडे!**.

**2. 'May it be…' = होस्; other verbs -ओस्.** For wishes about a thing or a third person: नयाँ वर्ष सुखमय **होस्** 'may the new year be happy', तपाईंको यात्रा सफल **होस्**, नयाँ जागिर **मिलोस्** 'may you find a new job'. With a plural or honorific subject, **-ऊन्**: भगवानले राम्रो **गरून्** 'may God bless you'.

**3. Blessings from an elder: -नू.** When an elder puts Dashain tika on you, the blessing is mostly a string of *deferred commands* in **-नू** — 'do this from now on': राम्रो **पढ्नू**, जागिर **पाउनू**, सधैँ खुसी **रहनू** 'study well, get a good job, always be happy'. To an adult they may switch to **-नुहोला**: सधैँ खुसी **रहनुहोला**.

**4. Wishing someone you respect: -नुहोस् / -नुहोला.** सधैँ स्वस्थ **रहनुहोस्** 'stay healthy always'. When an elder blesses you, you don't bless them back: bow (**ढोग**) or join your palms and smile.

examples.en: A very happy Tihar to you!
May the new year bring you happiness!
Study hard and make something of yourself. (Dashain blessing)

examples.native: भगवानले तपाईंहरूको जोडी सधैँ यस्तै राखून्।
examples.roman: bhagawānle tapāiṃharuko joḍi sadhaiṃ yastai rākhun.
examples.en: May God keep you two together always.

grammar.title: 'Be sure to…': -नू, पक्का, -नै पर्छ
grammar.body:
Nepali invitations come with insistence, and there are several ways to say 'be sure to…' or 'you simply must…'.

**-नू** (तिमी, unit 18) is the 'deferred' imperative, for something to do later: भोलि **आउनू** है 'be sure to come tomorrow'. Negative: **नबिर्सनू** 'don't forget'. For तपाईं: **-नुहोला**: **आउनुहोला** है.

**पक्का** 'for sure' before the verb makes it firmer: **पक्का आउनू**, **पक्का आउनुहोला**. The answer is **पक्का!** or **अवश्य!**.

**-नै पर्छ** 'you simply must': the -न form + **नै** + पर्छ: तिमी **आउनै पर्छ**! 'you HAVE to come!', यो सेलरोटी **खानै पर्छ** 'you've got to try this sel roti'. नै adds emphasis to -नुपर्छ (unit 15).

**नभुली** 'without fail' (lit. without forgetting): **नभुली** आउनुहोला.

The classic invitation is **…मा आउनुहोला है, पक्का!**. And the classic soft refusal is **कोसिस गर्छु** 'I'll try' — which often means no.

examples.en: You be sure to come too, OK?
Do come for tika tomorrow — no excuses!
You've simply got to try this sel roti!

examples.native: कोसिस गर्छु, तर पक्का भन्न सक्दिनँ।
examples.roman: kosis garchhu, tara pakkā bhanna sakdinaṃ.
examples.en: I'll try, but I can't promise.

grammar.title: The right verb for each festival
grammar.body:
English 'celebrate' covers everything; Nepali has a fixed verb for each activity, and using the right one makes you sound natural.

**मनाउनु** 'to celebrate': दसैं **मनाउनु**, जन्मदिन **मनाउनु**.
**टीका लगाउनु** 'to put tika on (someone)' — what the elder does · **टीका थाप्नु** 'to receive tika' — what you do: हजुरबुबाले टीका **लगाउनुभयो**, मैले टीका **थापेँ**.
**खेल्नु** 'to play' for Holi, swings and carol-singing: होली **खेल्नु**, पिङ **खेल्नु**, देउसी **खेल्नु**.
**दियो बाल्नु** 'to light lamps' · **माला लगाउनु** 'to garland (someone)' · **नाच्नु** 'to dance'.
**केक काट्नु** 'to cut the cake' · **मैनबत्ती निभाउनु** 'to blow out the candles'.
**बिहे गर्नु** 'to marry (someone)' — a transitive verb, so the doer takes ले in the past: उसले कलेजको साथीसँग बिहे **गर्‍यो** · **बिहे हुनु** 'to get married' (it happens to you): दिदीको बिहे **भयो**.
**खुवाउनु** 'to treat (someone to food)': good news means मिठाई **खुवाउनुपर्छ**.

At Dashain the elder puts red tika and **जमरा** on you and gives **दक्षिणा**; at Tihar sisters do **भाइटीका** for their brothers; at Teej women in red sing and dance.

examples.native: हामी हरेक वर्ष गाउँमा दसैं मनाउँछौँ।
examples.roman: hāmi harek barsa gāuṃmā dasaiṃ manāuṃchhauṃ.
examples.en: We celebrate Dashain in the village every year.
I received tika from my uncle too.
We played with colours with friends at Holi.
At Tihar, people light lamps in every house.

dialogue.title: A week before Dashain
dialogue.setting: Kathmandu, a week before Dashain. Sushma runs into her friend Nabin at New Road, where everyone is clothes-shopping.

lines.speaker: Sushma
lines.native: हो नि, सबैलाई नयाँ लुगा चाहियो। तिमी दसैंमा घर जाने हो?
lines.roman: ho ni, sabailāi nayāṃ lugā chāhiyo. timi dasaiṃmā ghar jāne ho?
lines.en: Yep, everyone needs new clothes. Are you going home for Dashain?

lines.speaker: Nabin
lines.native: अँ, फूलपातीको दिन पोखरा जान्छु। बस टिकट पाउनै गाह्रो!
lines.roman: aṃ, Phulpātiko din Pokharā jānchhu. bas ṭikaṭ pāunai gāhro!
lines.en: Yeah, I'm off to Pokhara on Phulpati. Getting a bus ticket is a nightmare!

lines.speaker: Sushma
lines.native: हाहा, सबै काठमाडौं खाली हुन्छ। अनि सुन न, मंसिरमा मेरो दिदीको बिहे छ!
lines.roman: hāhā, sabai Kāṭhmāḍauṃ khāli hunchha. ani suna na, mansirmā mero didiko bihe chha!
lines.en: Haha, the whole of Kathmandu empties out. Oh, and listen — my sister's getting married in Mangsir!

lines.speaker: Nabin
lines.native: साँच्चै? बधाई छ! केटा को हो?
lines.roman: sāṃchchai? badhāi chha! keṭā ko ho?

lines.speaker: Sushma
lines.native: धरानको हो, इन्जिनियर। लभ म्यारेज नि!
lines.roman: Dharānko ho, injiniyar. labh myārej ni!
lines.en: He's from Dharan, an engineer. A love marriage, mind you!

lines.speaker: Nabin
lines.native: वाह! मेहेन्दीमा नाच्न त म पनि आउँछु।
lines.roman: wāh! mehendimā nāchna ta ma pani āuṃchhu.
lines.en: Wow! Well, I'm coming to dance at the mehendi.

lines.speaker: Sushma
lines.native: आउनै पर्छ! निमन्त्रणा कार्ड पछि पठाउँछु। जन्ती धरानबाट आउँछ, रिसेप्सन कलङ्कीमा।
lines.roman: āunai parchha! nimantranā kārḍ pachhi paṭhāuṃchhu. janti Dharānbāṭa āuṃchha, risepsan Kalaṅkimā.
lines.en: You have to! I'll send the invitation card later. The groom's party is coming from Dharan, and the reception's in Kalanki.

lines.speaker: Nabin
lines.en: What should I give them, I wonder?

lines.speaker: Sushma
lines.native: केही पर्दैन, आशीर्वाद दिए पुग्छ। तर पक्का आउनू है!
lines.roman: kehi pardaina, āsirbād die pugchha. tara pakkā āunu hai!
lines.en: No need for anything, your blessing is enough. But be sure to come!

lines.speaker: Nabin
lines.native: पक्का! ल, दसैंको शुभकामना। जमरा र टीकाको फोटो पठाउनू!
lines.roman: pakkā! la, dasaiṃko subhakāmanā. jamarā ra ṭikāko phoṭo paṭhāunu!
lines.en: Definitely! Right, happy Dashain. Send me a photo of your tika and jamara!

lines.speaker: Sushma
lines.en: You too! Hope you get lots of dakshina!

culture:
**Dashain** (September–October) is the big one: offices close, and Kathmandu empties as everyone goes **घर** — to their home village or town — so bus tickets sell out days ahead. On the tenth day (**विजया दशमी**) elders put a red tika of rice, curd and vermilion on younger relatives' foreheads, tuck **जमरा** behind their ears, bless them and give **दक्षिणा**. People go from house to house for tika for several days, eating goat meat and sel roti everywhere. Kites fill the sky and villages put up huge bamboo swings (**पिङ**).

**Tihar** follows a few weeks later: crows, dogs and cows are honoured on successive days, houses are lit with **दियो** and fairy lights for Laxmi, the goddess of wealth, groups of young people go round singing **देउसी-भैलो** for money and food, and on **भाइटीका** sisters put a seven-coloured tika on their brothers and garland them with marigolds. **Teej** is the women's festival, with red saris, fasting and dancing at Pashupati; **Holi** is the colour festival; **ल्होसार** is celebrated by Tamang, Gurung and Sherpa communities; and Nepali New Year falls in mid-April (Bikram Sambat, about 57 years ahead of the Western calendar).

Wedding season is in the auspicious months (Mangsir, Magh, Falgun, Baisakh), when an astrologer fixes the **साइत**. A Hindu wedding has the **जन्ती** procession with a brass band (**पञ्चे बाजा**), the bride in red, **सिन्दूर** and the **पोते** necklace for married women, and an emotional **बिदाइ** when the bride leaves her parents' home. Guests at the reception give cash in a **लिफाफा** — the usual gift — and nobody expects you to stay long: eat, bless the couple, take a photo with them and go.

tip.title: 'Happy …!' and 'may it be…'
tip.body:
- 'Happy X!' = **X-को शुभकामना!**: दसैं**को शुभकामना**, जन्मदिन**को शुभकामना**.
- 'May it be…' = **होस्**; other verbs **-ओस्**: नयाँ जागिर मिल**ोस्**.
- With God or a plural subject: **-ऊन्**: भगवानले राम्रो गर**ून्**.

sentences.en: Happy Tihar, didi!
A very happy Lhosar!

sentences.native: यो दसैं सबैको लागि रमाइलो होस्!
sentences.roman: yo dasaiṃ sabaiko lāgi ramāilo hos!
sentences.en: May this Dashain be a joyful one for everyone!

sentences.native: नयाँ वर्षमा तिमीलाई नयाँ जागिर मिलोस्!
sentences.roman: nayāṃ barsamā timilāi nayāṃ jāgir milos!
sentences.en: May you find a new job in the new year!
May God bless everyone.
Happy Tihar to you and your family.
May everyone be well this year.

sentences.native: दसैं र तिहार हाम्रा सबैभन्दा ठूला चाडपर्व हुन्।
sentences.roman: dasaiṃ ra tihār hāmrā sabaibhandā ṭhulā chāḍparba hun.
sentences.en: Dashain and Tihar are our biggest festivals.
What are you doing for your birthday?

tip.title: Blessings from elders: -नू
tip.body:
- Elders bless younger people with the deferred command **-नू** 'do this from now on': राम्रो पढ्**नू**, सधैँ खुसी रह**नू**.
- To an adult: **-नुहोला**: खुसी रह**नुहोला**.
- You **receive** tika (टीका **थाप्नु**); the elder gives **दक्षिणा** and **जमरा**.

sentences.en: Study well, son.
Stay well always, dear.
May you get a job soon.
Keep smiling like this always.
Stay healthy always. (to an adult)
I received tika from Grandpa.
Put the jamara behind your ear, OK?
Grandma gave me five hundred rupees dakshina!

sentences.native: टीका थापेपछि सेलरोटी र मासु खाइन्छ।
sentences.roman: ṭikā thāpepachhi selroṭi ra māsu khāinchha.
sentences.en: After tika, people eat sel roti and meat.

sentences.native: यो दसैंमा घर जान्छौ कि काठमाडौंमै बस्छौ?
sentences.roman: yo dasaiṃmā ghar jānchhau ki Kāṭhmāḍauṃmai baschhau?
sentences.en: Are you going home this Dashain or staying in Kathmandu?

lessons.title: What you do at each festival

tip.title: The right verb for each festival
tip.body:
- **मनाउनु** 'celebrate': दसैं मनाउनु.
- **टीका लगाउनु** 'put tika on someone' — but **टीका थाप्नु** 'receive tika'.
- **खेल्नु** for Holi, swings and deusi: होली **खेल्नु**, पिङ **खेल्नु**, देउसी **खेल्नु**.
- **दियो बाल्नु** 'light lamps'.
tip.pattern: दसैं मनाउनु  ·  होली खेल्नु  ·  टीका थाप्नु

sentences.en: How do you guys celebrate Tihar?
Shall we go to Thamel to play Holi?
On Bhai Tika, sisters put tika on their brothers.
My sister put a garland on me.
At Tihar we light lamps at home.
At night the boys came round singing deusi.

sentences.native: तीजमा दिदीबहिनीहरू रातो सारी लगाएर नाच्छन्।
sentences.roman: tijmā didibahiniharu rāto sāri lagāera nāchchhan.
sentences.en: At Teej, women put on red saris and dance.
At Dashain a big swing is put up in the village.
Don't forget to come for Bhai Tika, little brother.

tip.title: 'Be sure to come!'
tip.body:
- **-नू** (तिमी) / **-नुहोला** (तपाईं): आउ**नू** है, आउ**नुहोला** है.
- **पक्का** makes it firmer: **पक्का** आउनू!
- **-नै पर्छ** 'you simply must': आउ**नै पर्छ**!, खा**नै पर्छ**!
- The soft no: **कोसिस गर्छु** 'I'll try'.

sentences.native: शनिबार मेरो जन्मदिनको पार्टी छ, पक्का आउनू।
sentences.roman: sanibār mero janmadinko pārṭi chha, pakkā āunu.
sentences.en: It's my birthday party on Saturday — be sure to come.
Please don't fail to come to the feast tomorrow. (polite)

sentences.native: यो केक खानै पर्छ, आमाले बनाउनुभएको!
sentences.roman: yo kek khānai parchha, āmāle banāunubhaeko!
sentences.en: You've got to try this cake — Mum made it!

sentences.native: तिमी आउनै पर्छ, नत्र म रिसाउँछु!
sentences.roman: timi āunai parchha, natra ma risāuṃchhu!
sentences.en: You have to come, or I'll be cross!

sentences.native: पास भयौ? अब सबैलाई मिठाई खुवाउनै पर्छ!
sentences.roman: pās bhayau? aba sabailāi miṭhāi khuwāunai parchha!
sentences.en: You passed? Now you've got to treat everyone to sweets!
Don't forget to cut the cake!
Do you absolutely have to give an envelope at a wedding?
Got the invitation card, thanks!
When is the auspicious date for the wedding?

sentences.native: केकमा कतिवटा मैनबत्ती राख्ने? गिफ्ट को ल्याउँछ?
sentences.roman: kekmā katiwaṭā mainbatti rākhne? giphṭ ko lyāuṃchha?
sentences.en: How many candles shall we put on the cake? Who's bringing the present?

tip.title: Talking about weddings
tip.body:
- **बिहे हुनु** 'get married' (it happens): दिदीको बिहे **भयो**.
- **बिहे गर्नु** 'marry (someone)' — doer + ले in the past: उसले बिहे **गर्‍यो**.
- Wish the couple **सुखी दाम्पत्य जीवनको शुभकामना!** (formal) or just **बधाई छ!**; compliment: **बेहुली कति राम्री!**
tip.pattern: X-को बिहे भयो  ·  X-ले बिहे गर्‍यो

sentences.en: My sister's getting married in Mangsir.
He married a friend from college.

sentences.native: जन्ती धरानबाट आउँछ, बिहे काठमाडौंमा हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: janti Dharānbāṭa āuṃchha, bihe Kāṭhmāḍauṃmā hunchha.
sentences.en: The groom's party is coming from Dharan; the wedding is in Kathmandu.
Where is the reception after the wedding?

sentences.native: उनीहरूको बिहे भएको दस वर्ष भयो।
sentences.roman: uniharuko bihe bhaeko das barsa bhayo.
sentences.en: They've been married for ten years.

sentences.native: बेहुला र बेहुलीलाई धेरै धेरै बधाई छ!
sentences.roman: behulā ra behulilāi dherai dherai badhāi chha!
sentences.en: Many congratulations to the bride and groom!

sentences.native: बेहुला त साँच्चै ह्यान्डसम छ नि!
sentences.roman: behulā ta sāṃchchai hyānḍsam chha ni!
sentences.en: The groom really is handsome!
After the wedding the bride wears sindur.
All the girls danced at the mehendi.
Mum cried when the bride left home.
